constraints_honored: live writemybook DB never dropped or altered
all destructive ops scoped to wmb_restore_drill only
no destructive calls against other personas' data

row_counts_first_pass_slow_loop.note: 43s verification loop against a live, concurrently-written dev DB; documents/edit_findings appeared off by 1 due to concurrent writes during the loop, not a restore defect (see tight_window_reconciliation)

tight_window_reconciliation.method: captured before_dump and after_dump counts bracketing a second, fresh pg_dump (1.306s runtime), then compared final restore against both baselines
tight_window_reconciliation.conclusion: restored counts match after_dump exactly (documents 86=86=86, edit_findings 85=85), consistent with pg_dump's MVCC snapshot capturing committed state through its own transaction start on a live, concurrently-written source DB. No restore-fidelity defect; discrepancy fully explained by concurrent writes from other QA agents.

byte_identical_spot_check.scope: chapters x documents metadata (chapter_number, title, word_count, status, beta_score, beta_gate, type, current_version, storage_key), ordered by chapter_number
byte_identical_spot_check.caveat: manuscript prose itself lives in MinIO/S3 object storage, not Postgres; this spot check verifies DB-side metadata identity only, not prose-byte identity of object storage content

gaps_for_production: credentials must come from secrets manager, not .env
RTO must be re-measured against realistic prod-sized data (this dev drill: 32 tables, ~196KB dump, <15s total)
requires maintenance window or blue/green cutover strategy for a live prod restore
should be wrapped in an idempotent, logged, alerting automation script rather than run by hand

constraints_honored: live wmb-projects bucket: read-only (list/GET only), never mutated
all destructive ops (mirror target, deletes) scoped to wmb-restore-drill-c2b only
no src/ edits, no server/worker restarts

object_count_reconciliation.conclusion: mismatch was ~37s of concurrent writes from other live QA agents during the mirror+list window, not a mirror-fidelity defect - same tight-window bracketing methodology as the Postgres drill

checksum_spot_check.method: ETag comparison (ETag = MD5 for single-part MinIO uploads) between source and throwaway-bucket copies

backed_up_bytes_vs_live_get_content_resp.read_path: DocumentService.readPinned() -> .versions/<documentId>/v<version>.md (versioned snapshot, not the mutable live storageKey)
backed_up_bytes_vs_live_get_content_resp.root_cause: artifact of my own curl+jq extraction pipeline on Windows: API response picked up CRLF line terminators (source S3 object is LF-only) plus one trailing blank line added by jq's raw-string extraction
backed_up_bytes_vs_live_get_content_resp.conclusion: live app serves byte-for-byte identical prose to the durably-stored version snapshot; no defect filed

restore_into_throwaway_bucket_drill.method: bucket-to-bucket s3 sync IS the restore drill (MinIO/S3 has no separate restore primitive distinct from mirror/copy)

object_storage_leg_c2b.ordering_constraint: Postgres documents.storage_key/DocumentVersion rows and S3 objects must be restored as a single consistent pair from the same (or compatible) point-in-time snapshot; the versioned-snapshot design (write-once, never deleted) means an object backup taken at-or-after the DB backup timestamp is guaranteed to contain every version the DB can reference - the mutable live-key path does not have this guarantee and needs same-instant pairing
gaps_for_production: Windows MAX_PATH hit on local-disk sync of deeply-nested .versions/<uuid>/vN.md keys - sandbox artifact only, worked around via bucket-to-bucket server-side mirror (also a better prod DR pattern than local-disk staging)

no automated reconciliation job exists to verify every documents.storage_key resolves to a present S3 object (or flag orphans) - should be added as a standing integrity check independent of the restore path
credentials/automation gaps mirror the Postgres leg's gaps_for_production list
